chunks: And the one who was saved from the two said, 'I will inform you of its interpretation; so let me go.'
ai.seo_question: Who offered to interpret the dreams in prison and what did he say?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the 'Fadila' (virtue) of the prison companion, often identified as one of the two prisoners who previously asked for interpretation, demonstrating his timely recall of Joseph's (AS) divine gift after a period of delay. His request for release ('Arsiluni') is viewed not merely as a logistical need but as a strategic move to present Joseph to the King, thereby fulfilling the destiny of the Prophet. This moment serves as a critical transition from obscurity to prominence, underscoring the theme of divine timing and the elevation of the righteous through patience.
